Thirty-eight reported points, worked through in one pass. The largest of them was not a look: a job could not be deleted at all.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A job could not be deleted, and the reason had two layers.** The editor changed its own list and never wrote the file, so a removal survived exactly until the next read. Underneath that, the validator refused a configuration with no jobs at all, so removing the ONLY job could never be saved even once saving was attempted. A fresh install has exactly one job, which is why this was reported against the only job there is. An empty job list is the state before the first job exists and after the last one goes; refusing it was defensible while the file was only ever hand-written and stopped being so the moment the interface could edit it.
- **The schedule lost its mode the moment you picked one.** Which mode was showing was read back out of the stored expression on every render, which works for every mode but the one that matters: entering the cron mode seeds the field from the schedule already set, so the stored string was something like `0 3 * * *` and reading it back said "daily". The picker jumped straight back the moment it was pressed. The same trap catches "every 24 hours" and "daily", which describe the same cadence and cannot be told apart from the expression alone.
- **The colour picker moved the live colour to a different swatch while it was still open.** Which slot held it was worked out from the colour itself, by nearest preset, on every render: nudge a colour far enough and it becomes nearer a different preset, so the selection jumped to another circle mid-drag. A slot being edited now keeps its colour however far you take it.
- **The motion switch could not reach a single animation.** It had three states and, apart from the progress bar, nothing to act on: the design language shipped its five animations with the durations written into the rules, so there was nothing for the setting to redefine. Measured rather than assumed, the page entrance ran at 280ms on full, on subtle and on off alike. Fixed in the language, so every app that copies it gains a switch that works.
- **The languages have real flags on Windows**, and the picker they sit in is the house one rather than the operating system's. Catalan, Galician and Basque get a flag for the first time.

## 🎨 Design

- **The text is the same size as in the other apps here.** Two real differences, both measured on the running apps rather than argued about: the body carried a size where the other one inherits the browser's, and the sizes that were classed were written as literal pixels one step below the same element there.
- **A selector segment carries the whole control radius** instead of the track's minus its padding, which had left it with under two pixels of rounding at the middle shape stage and made every horizontal selector read as square.
- **The settings strip reads as a tab bar.** Tabs, filter bars and segmented controls are one component here, so the difference is the scale, not the markup, and this strip was the one place opting out of the shared minimum width.
- **The appearance wording matches the other apps**, in all forty-two languages, lifted rather than re-invented: "Beschriftungen", "Buttons", "Seitenleiste", "Text und Symbol", "Regenbogen-Modus", "Reaktiver Modus", "Farbenrotation", "Farbpalette".
- **One card per job while editing it.** Opening a job used to leave its summary standing and add a second card underneath, so one job appeared twice with its name printed twice.
- **The delete window lost its second cancel button and both divider lines**, its confirm button gained a glyph, and it can now take the job's state database with it, which it does by default.
- **The direction control is two plain arrows** where it used to be a reload loop that draws hooks and reads as "retry".
- **Every button and every switch answers to the label engine and the colour engine.** The weekday buttons each take their own position in the palette, where they all carried the single accent, and the direction control was not in the label engine at all.

## ✨ Added

- **An "every N" schedule**, in minutes, hours, days or weeks. It counts from the last run rather than firing on the clock, so "every six hours" set at five o'clock means six hours from then.
- **A folder can be made from inside the folder picker**, instead of leaving it, making one elsewhere and coming back.
- **Registered drives and configured targets appear inside the picker**, at the top of its list, rather than in a second dropdown under the field.
- **A new job starts with sensible exclusions** rather than grey placeholder text that vanished at the first keystroke. Every one of them is a file the system or a tool rewrites on its own.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Renaming a job carries its state database along**, unless the path no longer looks like the generated one, in which case somebody moved it on purpose.
- **The storage form asks for what the chosen provider requires and nothing else.** For S3 that was fourteen boxes, most of them for one provider out of thirty; it asked about IBM resource instances before it asked for a key. Everything else is still one switch away.
- **The quiet period sits beside the schedule** and its explanation says what to type.
- **Name and state database line up with the two sides below them**, so the form has columns rather than four different widths.
- **The plus button is where a list's add button belongs**, top right and alone.
